criteria.rationale: The sequence uses acceptance as business completion, contradicting the settled-only rule; observation of subsequent states is also missing.

criteria.document_locator: A `202 Accepted` response confirms the payment has completed
criteria.rationale: 202 creates a queued payout. It does not establish settlement and can precede failure.

criteria.document_locator: That proves the invoice has been paid.
criteria.rationale: Checking only 202 cannot verify invoice payment. Sandbox state transitions and their expected observations are missing; no run is established.
No guidance at this anchor explains how to observe queued, settled or failed outcomes or keep an unsettled invoice unpaid.

findings.document_locator: A `202 Accepted` response confirms the payment has completed
findings.consequence: A merchant following the stated rule marks a queued or ultimately failed payout paid, hiding unpaid receivables from collection. The proposed sandbox check endorses the same false financial completion.
findings.fix: Explain that 202 acknowledges a queued request; mark only the invoice matching a settled payout paid. Replace the claim that checking 202 proves payment.

findings.consequence: Readers lack the observation and branch guidance needed to distinguish in-progress or failed payouts from settlement and to exercise those outcomes in sandbox.
findings.fix: Connect the returned payout ID to GET /payouts/{id} or payout.updated. Explain that queued is pending and failed is not paid; in sandbox use the fixture to drive settled and failed and observe each expected state. Do not claim the procedure was executed.
